item.title: 4: Daily Halacha: Why We Fast on the 10th of Tevet Part 1
item.description:
What makes the 10th of Tevet unique among the fasts? It can fall twice in one secular year and is the only fast that can fall on a Friday. Then the question of why we fast, with one reason being the translation of the Torah into Greek, which the Sages mourned.
Daily Halacha — Asarah BeTevet (Fast of the 10th of Tevet) Dayan Daniel Kada

item.title: 5: Daily Halacha: Why We Fast on the 10th of Tevet Part 2
item.description:
The Tenth of Tevet has more than one reason. Beyond the Torah's translation into Greek, the main reason is the start of the siege that led to the destruction of the first Temple, a fast from the Divrei Neviim, with the death of Ezra the scribe on the ninth of Tevet added as well.

item.title: 6: Daily Halacha: Waiting Until Nightfall on Friday to Eat, or Eating Once Shabbat Is Accepted
item.description:
Asarah BeTevet is the only fast that can fall on Erev Shabbat, so does it end at nightfall or when Shabbat is accepted? Rishonim divide. The Shulhan Arukh requires fasting until nightfall, the Rama lets a private fast end after Arvit, and a public fast must wait.
Daily Halacha — Asarah BeTevet (Fast of the 10th of Tevet) Dayan Daniel Kada

item.title: 7: Daily Halacha: Eating and Drinking Before the Fast Begins
item.description:
When exactly does the Asarah BeTevet fast begin? Unlike Tisha BeAv, it starts at dawn, which Sephardim take as 72 minutes before sunrise, giving 6.54 that Friday, with some stringent at 90 minutes. Whether one may eat or drink on waking depends on whether one stipulated the night before.
Daily Halacha — Asarah BeTevet (Fast of the 10th of Tevet) Dayan Daniel Kada

item.title: 8: Daily Halacha: Birkat HaKohanim on Fast Days
item.description:
Why is Birkat Kohanim said at Minhah on a fast day, but not on a regular afternoon or on Yom Kippur? The concern is that a Kohen must not be drunk, so the custom applies only when Minhah is prayed at the very end of the day, as at Neilah on a fast.
Daily Halacha — Asarah BeTevet (Fast of the 10th of Tevet) Dayan Daniel Kada

item.title: 9: Daily Halacha: Can One Brush One's Teeth on a Fast?
item.description:
Is brushing teeth on a minor fast like drinking? The Shulhan Arukh says rinsing the mouth is not fitting on a fast day. For the 17th of Tammuz, Fast of Gedaliah and 10th of Tevet, later authorities permit it with the head tilted down and under a revit, about 86 millilitres, of water.
Daily Halacha — Asarah BeTevet (Fast of the 10th of Tevet) Dayan Daniel Kada

item.title: 10: Daily Halacha: Kosher Restaurants Opening on Fast Days
item.description:
Does serving a customer on a fast day count as a stumbling block before the blind? The prohibition of placing a stumbling block before the blind applies only to a Torah-level sin, and here the customer's eating is not, and he could sin without the restaurant. So restaurants may open, and a reminder sign is a good idea.
Daily Halacha — Asarah BeTevet (Fast of the 10th of Tevet) Dayan Daniel Kada

item.title: 11: Daily Halacha: Eating Before the Fast
item.description:
May one eat or drink before a fast begins if awake before dawn? The Rabbi covers Ovadia Yosef's calculation of dawn, the Gemara's rule that going to sleep counts as accepting the fast unless a condition is made, and the differing views of Shulhan Arukh and Rema on drinking.

item.title: 1: Daily Halacha: The History of the Fast of Tevet Part 1
item.description:

item.title: 2: Daily Halacha: The History of the Fast of Tevet Part 2
item.description:
Why is the tenth of Tevet a sad day, and what else does Megillat Taanit mark in those days? Part 2 covers the death of Ezra the scribe on the ninth, his role in continuing the Mesorah and ending intermarriage, and the siege of Yerushalayim on the tenth, together with the translation of the Torah into Greek.

item.title: 12: Daily Halacha: Fast of Tevet Which Falls on Friday: Making Kiddush Before Nightfall
item.description:
When may one break the fast if the Tenth of Tevet falls on Friday? The Rosh and the Maharam of Rottenberg allow eating after accepting Shabbat, but the Shulhan Arukh says to wait for nightfall. Those in need have much to rely on; a private fast differs.

item.title: 3: Daily Halacha: A Thought for the 10th of Tevet: Seeking the Roots of Dark Times
item.description:
Why do we fast on the tenth of Tevet for a mere siege, when other fasts mark the Temple in flames? The siege was the root from which the destruction grew. The talk asks us to study the roots of dark times, and links this to 7 October.
